title: Statins: very infrequent reports of myasthenia gravis
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: MHRA Drug Safety Update, volume 17, issue 2, September 2023
funder: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
result: Following a European review (PRAC, January 2023), the product information of all statins is being updated to list myasthenia gravis and ocular myasthenia as adverse reactions of unknown frequency, with new warnings. Globally there has been a very small number of reports of new-onset or aggravated myasthenia gravis with atorvastatin, pravastatin, lovastatin, fluvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin and pitavastatin. From 14 June 1995 to 19 June 2023 the MHRA received 10 UK Yellow Card reports (simvastatin, atorvastatin, pravastatin), against more than 9.5 million UK patients dispensed a statin in 2022 alone; median age 66 years (40 to 89); symptoms included double vision, difficulty with speech and swallowing, limb weakness and shortness of breath; onset a few days to three months after starting; three reports concerned recurrence or exacerbation in known myasthenia gravis, one a positive rechallenge; four patients were hospitalised; no fatal UK reports. Most UK reports note recovery after stopping, a minority continued to have symptoms, and recurrence has been reported on restarting the same or a different statin. Data are insufficient to determine whether statin, duration or dose alter the risk, or whether new-onset disease is transient or permanent.
